context.objective: Understand instructions about sorting waste and recycling at an exhibition.
context.conversationContext: Authored reading snapshot, not a current news claim.

sourceMaterial.passageHanzi: 展览结束后，请分类投放垃圾。纸张可以回收利用，所以请放进回收箱。
sourceMaterial.passageMeaning: After the exhibition, please sort the waste into the appropriate bins. Paper can be recycled, so please put it in the recycling bin.

targets.meaning: sort and put into the appropriate bins

sources.title: 分类投放 — learning card
sources.excerpt: 分类投放 (fēn lèi tóu fàng) — sort and put into the appropriate bins. Sense: sort and put into the appropriate bins. Assessed skill: recognition.

sources.title: 回收利用 — learning card
sources.excerpt: 回收利用 (huí shōu lì yòng) — recycle and reuse. Sense: recycle and reuse. Assessed skill: recognition.

sources.title: Authored evaluation snapshot (not retrieved)
sources.excerpt:
展览结束后，请分类投放垃圾。纸张可以回收利用，所以请放进回收箱。
After the exhibition, please sort the waste into the appropriate bins. Paper can be recycled, so please put it in the recycling bin.

graph.overview: Understand that 分类投放 means sorting waste into the correct bins before disposal. Understand that 回收利用 means recycling and reusing materials, and recognize how the passage uses it to justify placing paper in the recycling bin.

waypoints.objective: Understand that 分类投放 means sorting waste into the correct bins before disposal.
waypoints.explanation: The phrase 分类投放 combines 分类 (sort by category) and 投放 (put into a designated place). In this exhibition context, it is an instruction to separate different types of waste before placing them in their matching bins, rather than dumping everything together.
waypoints.exampleMeaning: Please sort the waste into the appropriate bins.

waypoints.objective: Understand that 回收利用 means recycling and reusing materials, and recognize how the passage uses it to justify placing paper in the recycling bin.
waypoints.explanation: The phrase 回收利用 combines 回收 (recover/reclaim) and 利用 (utilize), meaning to recycle and reuse. In the passage, it appears in the clause 纸张可以回收利用 (paper can be recycled and reused). This clause provides the reason for the subsequent instruction: because paper is recyclable, it should be placed in the recycling bin (回收箱). Understanding this cause-and-effect link is essential for interpreting the full recycling instruction.
waypoints.exampleHanzi: 纸张可以回收利用，所以请放进回收箱。
waypoints.exampleMeaning: Paper can be recycled and reused, so please put it in the recycling bin.

context.proposedDirections: 1. Check the cause-and-effect link in w2: A visitor holds a plastic bottle and asks if it can be recycled. The learner must select a reply that correctly distinguishes it from the paper instruction (e.g., stating it is not paper or directing it to a different bin), demonstrating understanding that 回收利用 specifically justifies the paper action in the source. 2. Check the scope of the instruction in w1: A visitor asks if they can throw all waste into one bin after the exhibition. The learner must select a reply that enforces the 分类投放 requirement, rejecting the idea of mixed disposal and affirming the need to sort waste into appropriate bins as per the notice. 3. Check the conditional timing in w1: A visitor asks about waste disposal during the exhibition (before it ends). The learner must select a reply that clarifies the instruction applies after the exhibition ends (展览结束后), ensuring the temporal condition of the sorting instruction is respected.

practiceQuestions.stem: At the exhibition, a visitor holds a piece of paper and asks where to put it. Which reply correctly applies the sorting instruction from the notice?
practiceQuestions.passage: 展览结束后，请分类投放垃圾。纸张可以回收利用，所以请放进回收箱。

wireContent.text:
I will select proposed direction 2 to check the scope of the instruction in waypoint w1 (分类投放). This direction tests whether the learner understands that waste must be sorted into appropriate bins, rather than mixed together, which is the core meaning of the target phrase.

<tool_call>
function=build_question_answers
<parameter=stem>
At the exhibition, a visitor asks if they can throw all their waste into one bin. Which reply correctly enforces the sorting instruction from the notice?
</parameter>
<parameter=passage>
展览结束后，请分类投放垃圾。纸张可以回收利用，所以请放进回收箱。
</parameter>
<parameter=answerA>
请分类投放垃圾。
</parameter>
<parameter=answerB>
请放进回收箱。
</parameter>
<parameter=answerC>
纸张可以回收利用。
</parameter>
<parameter=answerD>
展览结束后。
</parameter>
<parameter=correct>
A
</parameter>
<parameter=feedback>
The correct reply is "请分类投放垃圾" (Please sort the waste into the appropriate bins). This directly addresses the visitor's question about mixing waste by enforcing the requirement to sort it. "请放进回收箱" (Please put it in the recycling bin) is too specific and only applies to recyclable items like paper, not all waste. "纸张可以回收利用" (Paper can be recycled) explains a reason but does not give the instruction to sort. "展览结束后" (After the exhibition) only states the timing, not the action required.
</parameter>
<parameter=waypointIds>
["w1"]
</parameter>
<parameter=cardId>
evaluation-card-1
</parameter>
<parameter=intent>
Check the scope of the instruction in w1: A visitor asks if they can throw all waste into one bin after the exhibition. The learner must select a reply that enforces the 分类投放 requirement, rejecting the idea of mixed disposal and affirming the need to sort waste into appropriate bins as per the notice.
</parameter>
<parameter=whyMissing>
The practice question focuses on the specific action for paper (w2/recycling bin). This check question focuses on the general sorting instruction (w1/classification) to ensure the learner distinguishes between the general rule of sorting and the specific rule for recyclables.
</parameter>
</function></tool_call>
